title: Capitalize or Expense When In-Service Date Crosses the Threshold Change
scenario_text:
Vinson Semiconductors accounts for equipment purchases under its Fixed Asset Capitalization Policy.

Version 1 (in effect through 2024-09-30): "Equipment with a unit cost of $5,000 or more is capitalized and depreciated straight-line over 5 years. Items below $5,000 are expensed as incurred."

Version 2 (effective 2024-10-01): "The capitalization threshold is raised to $10,000, and capitalized equipment is depreciated straight-line over 3 years. Items below $10,000 are expensed." Version 2 adds a transition clause: "The capitalization policy applied to an asset is the version in effect on the asset's in-service date (the date it is placed in service), not the purchase-order date or the invoice date. Assets placed in service before October 1, 2024 follow v1."

The fixed-asset subledger shows asset candidate AC-2205 (a bench inspection unit): Purchase Order Date 2024-09-15, Invoice Date 2024-09-28, In-Service Date 2024-10-05, Unit Cost $7,500, Quantity 1. The receiving log confirms the unit was delivered 2024-09-30 but sat uncommissioned until calibration completed on 2024-10-05, which the subledger records as the in-service date. No component of the cost was expensed at receipt, and the asset remains in a pending clearing account awaiting the accountant's determination. The purchasing record shows a single line item with no bundled installation or freight charges added to the unit cost.

A staff accountant emails the assistant controller on 2024-10-08: "Booking AC-2205, unit cost $7,500. It was ordered and invoiced in September, so I was going to capitalize it over 5 years under the old $5,000 rule. But it wasn't placed in service until October 5. How should this be treated, and if it is capitalized, over what useful life?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the subledger record, determine the correct accounting treatment for AC-2205.
question: How should AC-2205 be accounted for?
choices: Expense the $7,500 in the period incurred: v2 governs by the 2024-10-05 in-service date, and $7,500 is below v2's $10,000 capitalization threshold.
Capitalize the $7,500 and depreciate it straight-line over 5 years, because the 2024-09-28 invoice date falls under v1's $5,000 threshold.
Capitalize the $7,500 and depreciate it straight-line over 3 years, because v2 governs by the 2024-10-05 in-service date.
Capitalize the $7,500 and depreciate it straight-line over 5 years, because the 2024-09-15 purchase-order date falls under v1.
Split the cost: capitalize the portion above $5,000 and expense the remainder.
